transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-04-02 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Emma Chen (Redwood AE), Mateo Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Kumar (Head of ML, Orion), Daniel Park (Infra), Maya Lopez (CTO)

Summary (auto): quick product walkthrough of Redwood Optimize focusing on quantization profiles. Discussed INT8 and FP8 tradeoffs, how Optimize measures quality regressions using prompt sets, and logistics for running a customer benchmark.

00:00:04 Emma Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm emma from redwood, mateo and i will run through Optimize quantization profiles today, hope that's still the plan
00:00:12 Priya Kumar: yeah thanks emma, we - yeah excited, we've been seeing costs edge up on some high-volume endpoints so curious about INT8/FP8 options
00:00:24 Mateo Alvarez: cool, quick agenda: how optimize profiles are generated, quality vs latency graphs, demo of the profiling run, then Q&A and next steps. we'll also talk about dedicated vs hosted behavior under quantization
00:00:40 Maya Lopez: quick note from me - security and KMS are gating for us if we go beyond hosted, so will want SOC2 and KMS details
00:00:51 Emma Chen: absolutely, we'll include SOC2 and KMS docs. okay starting slides - so Optimize runs a short eval over your representative prompt set and compares baseline fp16/fp32 outputs to quantized variants, we support int8 and fp8 profiles today
00:01:12 Daniel Park: small clarifying q: when you say fp8, is that dynamic range fp8 or a specific vendor implementation?
00:01:20 Mateo Alvarez: good question. it's a vendor-agnostic fp8-ish emulation path in our runtime plus some hardware-accelerated kernels where available; we'll call out exact kernel mappings in the report, sometimes it maps to vendor fp8 modes on A100X or future hw
00:01:39 Priya Kumar: and the quality metric - what do you use? bleu/rouge, embedding distance, or manual eval?
00:01:46 Mateo Alvarez: we do task-flexible metrics - by default we compute normalized embedding cosine deltas for semantic tasks and token-level logprob deltas for generation; Optimize also surfaces downsampled human-eval style pass/fail if you upload label sets
00:02:05 Emma Chen: i'll share the benchmark spreadsheet that has all the metrics columns we use so you can see exact thresholds
00:02:14 Priya Kumar: perfect.
00:02:18 Mateo Alvarez: jumping into the demo - here's an example profile run: baseline is fp16 with baseline latency and quality, int8 tends to reduce memory and token compute such that p50/p95 latencies drop by roughly 15-30% depending on sequence length and batching. fp8 often gives a larger memory win and can be more cost-efficient, but it's slightly more variable on quality for some decoder-only models
00:02:46 Emma Chen: note that these numbers vary a lot by model and prompt distribution; Optimize recommends a profile and then flags prompts where the quality delta exceeds tolerances so you can review
00:02:59 Daniel Park: can you show how caching interacts? we use prefix caching heavily so curious if quantization hurts KV cache performance
00:03:08 Mateo Alvarez: prefix/KV cache is orthogonal - the cache stores logits and KV in the runtime format, quantization affects the compute kernels and weight storage. in practice we see the cache hit latency remains stable; the per-token compute after cache lookup is where int8/fp8 gives the speedup. there are a few edge cases with extreme prompt lengths where the kernel selection changes
00:03:35 Priya Kumar: okay that helps. what about hallucination/regression risks - have you seen any categories of prompts that degrade more with fp8?
00:03:42 Mateo Alvarez: yes, low-temperature factual recall plus math-style tokens sometimes show higher divergence under aggressive quant; Optimize flags those and we recommend fallback policies - e.g., route those prompts to fp16 or to a quality-first variant for that route
00:04:01 Emma Chen: we also have rollout controls in the console so you can canary - start with 10% traffic on int8 profile then monitor quality metrics and roll up or rollback
00:04:12 Maya Lopez: that's useful - we'll need the canary and tracing info for audits
00:04:18 Emma Chen: noted, we'll include the tracing hooks doc.
00:04:26 Mateo Alvarez: moving on - demo: here's Optimize's UI showing the quality vs latency scatter; each dot is a sample prompt from your set, x-axis = latency p50, y-axis = normalized quality delta, color = model variant. you can click a dot to see original and quantized outputs side-by-side
00:04:48 Daniel Park: i like the side-by-side, that helps non-ML stakeholders review regressions
00:04:55 Priya Kumar: can i upload a label set to get pass/fail?
00:04:59 Mateo Alvarez: yes, we support labeled evals - it becomes an extra column in the report and we can synthesize an aggregate pass rate per variant
00:05:12 Emma Chen: quick question - what's your latency SLO and cost target? that helps us set tolerances
00:05:18 Priya Kumar: target p95 is under 400ms for conversational product and cost needs to be down about 30% vs current spend for the high-volume embeddings route
00:05:30 Emma Chen: great, we'll run the profile with those SLOs and highlight candidate profiles that hit your cost reduction while keeping quality in threshold
00:05:40 Mateo Alvarez: demo continued - here's a generated report, see the quality-latency Pareto frontier, we mark the knee points for int8 and fp8. for example, int8 might hit your latency SLO with minimal quality loss; fp8 might be slightly faster/cost cheaper but flagged on 3% of prompts for quality review
00:06:02 Priya Kumar: 3% is borderline for us, depends on which prompts - can we map flagged prompts back to product intents?
00:06:09 Mateo Alvarez: yes, Optimize annotates intents if you provide intent metadata in upload; otherwise it's by prompt id and text so you can map it post-run
00:06:21 Maya Lopez: what about dedicated/private deployment differences - do you see different behavior on our on-prem GPUs vs your hosted clusters?
00:06:30 Emma Chen: behavior is largely runtime-kernel dependent; on-prem kernels and driver versions can affect fp8 mappings. for Dedicated we provision the hardware and run the same profiling flow, we'll note any kernel mismatches in the report and recommend a compatible build or microkernel change
00:06:48 Daniel Park: will you need admin access to our infra for the Dedicated trial?
00:06:53 Emma Chen: typically no, we'll give you a trial endpoint on a dedicated pool we control; for on-prem Private installs we work with your infra team for an air-gapped package. we'll coordinate the least-privilege install if you go that route
00:07:08 Priya Kumar: fine. on the trial, can we limit it to specific routes? we have a few high-volume routes but also experimental ones
00:07:13 Emma Chen: yes, route-level controls are supported - we can pin specific model+profile combos to routes and set canaries per route
00:07:22 Mateo Alvarez: back to quality metrics, you'll also get token-level logprob deltas so you can see if divergences are concentrated in stop tokens or factual anchors
00:07:33 Priya Kumar: useful.
00:07:36 Emma Chen: i'm going to demo a quick live profiling run now - Mateo will kick off a sample job using a small curated prompt set we prepared earlier (demo data, names obfuscated)
00:07:47 Mateo Alvarez: starting job - this will run 120 samples across baseline and int8/fp8 variants, estimate about 10 minutes for the run in our dedicated trial pool but quicker on smaller sets. i'll narrate results as they stream
00:08:03 [00:08:03] Mateo Alvarez: streaming results - p50 baseline 180ms, int8 p50 145ms, fp8 p50 130ms (these are illustrative numbers for demo)
00:08:18 Priya Kumar: okay those deltas look promising
00:08:22 Mateo Alvarez: quality scatter - most points cluster around <0.5% embedding delta for int8, fp8 has a fatter tail with ~2-3% of prompts above the 1.5% threshold
00:08:36 Daniel Park: what do you mean by threshold? can we tune that?
00:08:40 Mateo Alvarez: yes you set the threshold in Optimize when you run a profile - by default we default to conservative thresholds but customers who want more aggressive cost savings can relax thresholds and accept more flagged prompts
00:08:52 Emma Chen: also you can configure automated fallback rules - e.g., if a prompt is flagged, route to fp16 for that request or run a second-pass verification
00:09:02 Maya Lopez: curious about billing during the trial - will int8/fp8 runs be billed differently?
00:09:08 Emma Chen: billing is per token but we show estimated unit cost per profile in the report; during the trial we'll annotate compute-time and token counts so you can estimate monthly impact. Dedicated contracts can be structured with reserved capacity pricing to make this predictable
00:09:24 Priya Kumar: ok good.
00:09:28 Mateo Alvarez: streaming more details - here's the side-by-side diff for sample id 23, you can see the fp8 output inserts a slightly different entity name, probability delta on token 12 is -2.4% so it's flagged
00:09:45 Priya Kumar: any ways to automatically patch or normalize that? like entity canonicalization post-process?
00:09:52 Mateo Alvarez: yes, some customers implement post-processing (e.g., entity normalization) when they know the risk categories. Optimize can surface likely categories so you can choose to patch or fall back
00:10:06 Emma Chen: running towards Q&A - Priya, you previously mentioned embeddings route as high volume; int8/FP8 on embeddings, we've seen big cost wins. note embeddings quantization is different - we usually quantize weight matmuls but preserve float output for similarity stability; Optimize has a separate embeddings profile
00:10:30 Priya Kumar: good to know. how do you validate retrieval quality after quantized embeddings?
00:10:36 Mateo Alvarez: we compute recall@k on a labeled dev set and embedding cosine stability metrics; if recall drops beyond threshold we mark it as a fail for that profile
00:10:46 Daniel Park: are the Optimize runs reproducible? we'd like an auditable trail for compliance
00:10:51 Emma Chen: yes, every run produces an exportable report, hashes of model weights used, kernel versions, and you can store run metadata in your audit logs. we'll include log export options to your S3 or to your SIEM if needed
00:11:08 Maya Lopez: good. any gotchas on long context lengths? some of our prompts go to 16k tokens
00:11:14 Mateo Alvarez: for long context, the memory/layouts change and kernel selection can flip; int8 still gives wins but you may see less relative speedup because KV memory dominates. Optimize simulates your seq distribution to pick the correct kernels
00:11:30 Priya Kumar: okay that's helpful.
00:11:34 Emma Chen: quick recap - we'll (1) run a customer-specific profiling job using your prompt set with the SLOs you gave, (2) share the benchmark sheet and report including flagged prompts, (3) provision a trial dedicated slot and run end-to-end, (4) share SOC2/KMS and tracing docs.
00:11:56 Priya Kumar: yes that aligns - we'll upload prompts today and aim to review results next week
00:12:03 Maya Lopez: one more question on fallbacks - is routing instant or do you need to wait for a new model spin?
00:12:08 Mateo Alvarez: routing is policy-based at request time - we can route by model variant, by profile tag, or by per-prompt decision. so instant on the software side, no model spin required
00:12:20 Daniel Park: cool.
00:12:23 Emma Chen: okay we'll follow up with the artifacts and calendar invite for the deep dive. thanks everyone for your time.
00:12:30 Priya Kumar: thanks all.

Notes about transcript: transcription contains some disfluencies and a few misrecognized vendor names; speaker labels are accurate for the most part but there are short sections where speaker turns are merged. The demo run numbers were illustrative and will be replaced by customer-specific results in the follow-up report.
